hypotheses.note: E0-manifolds only (T-btz-scope, needs-ruling; DEC-116 (b), DEC-125 (a)(e)); T2, connected, second countable as in every lean-gx E0 row (DEC-66). For E0, Reg_{>0} M = Reg M = E0LM.e0RegM M.

hypotheses.paper: Cauchy-complete (l.227: a smooth spacelike Cauchy surface which is metrically complete)
hypotheses.note: IsE0C1CompleteCauchy: the data of DEC-31/119's GX.IsE0CauchyComplete on S (implied: IsE0C1CompleteCauchy.isE0CauchyComplete) plus 'smooth' read as DEC-107 reads it for Cauchy-compact (the C1 rim field of E0Surgery.IsE0C1SpacelikeCauchy, verbatim). Used only by the Cauchy-completeness conclusion, which is the open sorry.
Causal.Flat.MGH (e0RegMFlat M): every flat Cauchy embedding of Reg M (into a FlatSpacetime.{0} 2) is onto

sorries.obstruction: The non-compact surgery. E0Surgery.SurgeryData has finitely many spears (field finite, from compactness: l.1091 'Since M is Cauchy-compact, it admits finitely many BTZ-lines'), and exists_surgeryData, SurgeryData.isCauchySurface_sigmaStar, completeSpace_sigmaStar all take a compact IsE0C1SpacelikeCauchy surface, so none applies to a complete S, which may carry countably many BTZ points (discrete and closed in S, kb/0217). Owed: (1) a countable, locally finite family of pairwise disjoint closed spears around S ∩ sing0 M, each with S's trace a C1 circle in its shaft (Lemmas tube, add_BTZ_param); (2) Sigma* Cauchy in Reg M with infinitely many spears (cor:intersect in each spear, plus local finiteness for an inextensible curve meeting infinitely many spears); (3) Sigma* complete for its induced length: Lemma 2.8's log r estimate inside each spear and a comparison across infinitely many spears (perhaps uniform, perhaps avoidable, AUDIT-1), with the DEC-31 length of S outside them. The paper prints none of this ('applies as is').

findings: l.1571 ('the proof of Cauchy-completeness of Proposition prop:abs_max applies as is'): it does not apply as is. That proof (l.1091) uses that a Cauchy-compact M has finitely many BTZ lines, so finitely many disjoint spears and one surgery each. A Cauchy-complete M may have countably many BTZ lines, and then the completeness of Sigma* with infinitely many spears is not addressed by the paper (a uniform estimate is one route; with locally finite spears a Hopf–Rinow-type argument may avoid it — AUDIT-1). This is a gap in the proof, not a counterexample: I found no counterexample and expect the statement to hold.

l.1571–1575 (Cauchy-maximality): the paper's route goes through the surgered Sigma* (lem:curve_extension (ii), cor:intersect, l.1574–1575), and it is not needed. Proved here (GX.E0RegComplete.gh_mgh_regM, standard axioms): for EVERY globally hyperbolic Cauchy-maximal E0-manifold M with a Cauchy surface, Reg M is globally hyperbolic and Cauchy-maximal. Cauchy-completeness and smoothness are not used. Route: the push-out M̄ of lem:extension_hausdorff is globally hyperbolic (the proof of prop:abs_max does not use compactness: E0MixedDiamond.globallyHyperbolic_pushout); ι₁(M) is causally convex in M̄; the image of ANY Cauchy surface of M is then a Cauchy surface of M̄, by Sbierski's union argument (Causal.CBG.isCauchySurfaceOn_sup_of_slice).

l.1573 ('We are left to show M → M̄ is a Cauchy-extension'): the argument printed at l.1574–1575 never shows that Σ stays acausal in M̄, and the Cauchy property needs it. Here it comes from the causal convexity of ι₁(M) in M̄ (causallyConvexIn_range_ι₁), which has three ingredients: the past of a BTZ point is BTZ; an earlier point of a BTZ line is chronologically below every regular point of the later point's future (DEC-64's Iplus_of_lt); and the image of a flat Cauchy embedding is causally convex (causallyConvexIn_range_of_isFlatCauchyEmbedding).
questions: Cauchy-complete for an E0-manifold (l.227: 'a smooth spacelike Cauchy-surface … metrically complete'). Reading taken: DEC-31/119's GX.IsE0CauchyComplete (spacelike Lipschitz in Reg M's flat charts, complete for the induced length extended across the BTZ lines), with 'smooth' read as DEC-107 reads it for Cauchy-compact, i.e. the C1 rim condition of IsE0C1SpacelikeCauchy. The rim condition goes beyond DEC-31/119, so this needs an OQ row: is the C1 rim reading of 'smooth' accepted for Cauchy-complete as it was for Cauchy-compact? It is consumed only by the open Cauchy-completeness clause.

Cauchy-maximal for Reg M (l.1568). Reading taken: Causal.Flat.MGH, i.e. Cauchy-maximal among flat spacetimes. The paper's 'Cauchy-extension N of M*' (l.1572) is an E_{>=0}-manifold, but a Cauchy extension of a spacetime with no singular line has none: each singular line is inextensible and would cross the image of a Cauchy surface. So the two readings agree, though that equivalence is not formalized here. An E0-target form (IsE0CauchyMaximal of Reg M) is not stated.
Scope: E0 only, as for every btz row anchored in lean-gx (T-btz-scope, needs-ruling). For E0-manifolds Reg_{>0} M = Reg M.

kb_proposals: E0Pushout forgets that ι₂ : FlatE0 N → M̄ is an E0-morphism, and the curve-level transport needs it (only le_ι₂ on range ι₂ survives). Use GX.E0RegComplete.exists_e0Pushout_mor, which is exists_e0Pushout's construction returning that property as well.

Cauchy-maximality of Reg M needs no surgery: push-out GH + causal convexity of ι₁(M) + Causal.CBG.isCauchySurfaceOn_sup_of_slice (GX.E0RegComplete.mgh_regM). Do not rebuild Sigma* to prove maximality.

The image of a flat Cauchy embedding is causally convex: Causal.Causality.causallyConvexIn_of_isCauchySurfaceOn with flatCausality_causallyArcConnected 2 N and Causal.CBG.flat_curvesExtend (GX.E0RegComplete.causallyConvexIn_range_of_isFlatCauchyEmbedding).
notes: One tagged sorry (regM_isCauchyComplete_of_complete); prop_reg_complete and prop_reg_complete' rest on it. gh_mgh_regM, mgh_regM, isCauchySurface_pushout and causallyConvexIn_range_ι₁ are sorry-free on standard axioms. exists_e0Pushout_mor copies the 110-line proof of E0AbsMax.exists_e0Pushout verbatim and adds the ι₂ property. At graduation, prefer adding that field to E0Pushout (or exporting hι) over keeping the copy. The import line sits directly after T-btz-embeddings' line in GXScaffold.lean. Imports only GX.* (no Causal.* import, kb/0030).
